summary: Store plan step 5: encrypted transport for the phones. The desktop phone endpoint and the headless server mint one self-signed certificate per install (data dir, tls/), reuse it across restarts, and serve wss:// and ws:// on the same port (the first byte of a connection picks TLS or plain). The pairing QR keeps its ws:// address and adds the certificate's SHA-256 as fp, so older phones ignore it and keep ws://. Native Android pins fp, dials wss:// on the same port, treats a changed certificate as a terminal error that asks for a re-pair, and in release builds refuses plain ws:// to any host but loopback and the emulator host (network security config and a clear message). New Expo iOS binaries use an Apple-only local Expo module backed by URLSessionWebSocketTask to pin the QR leaf certificate SHA-256, upgrading pinned addresses to wss:// on the same port. A mismatch is terminal with the same re-pair message as Android. Store builds still refuse remote ws:// without fp. Optional native lookup preserves the old gate in Expo Go and older binaries; fingerprint runtimeVersion includes the native module and prevents this OTA reaching old binaries. IAP, stored URLs, credentials, package identity and signing are unchanged.

automated: vitest tests/unit/backend-tls.test.ts: the certificate verifies against its own key, its SHA-256 matches the stored fingerprint, the key file is 0600, a restart reuses it and an unreadable one is replaced; one port answers ws:// and wss:// with the pinned certificate; close releases the port for a restart.
vitest tests/unit/transport-security.test.ts: the QR URL carries fp, the Expo parser keeps it lowercase and refuses a malformed one, and the cleartext rule allows only wss://, loopback and 10.0.2.2.
jest apps/mobile transport-gate.test.ts: an App Store build refuses remote ws:// before any dial and shows the reason, an internal build dials as before, an unreadable build type fails closed.

Gradle :app:testDebugUnitTest: PinnedTlsTest dials a MockWebServer over TLS with a certificate made by the desktop generator (match opens, mismatch is CertificateChangedFailure), pairing parse upgrades a pinned ws:// QR to wss://, the resolver refuses remote ws:// in release mode, and the status copy for a changed certificate.
Gradle lintDebug assembleRelease: the release APK packs the TLS-only network security config, debug the permissive one.
npm run typecheck and npm test pass.

iOS Jest: pinned socket selection, optional module absence, platform isolation, per-socket event routing and cleanup, auth/hello framing through the real transport, and terminal pin failure without retries. The store gate allows pinned URLs only when the native module is available.

Expo prebuild -p ios --no-install succeeded; generated ios/ moved outside the worktree. Expo autolinking resolves SwitchboardPinnedWebSocket and fingerprint sources include modules/pinned-websocket/ios.
PinnedSocket.swift compiled with swiftc for arm64-apple-ios16.4 using the iPhoneOS SDK, producing an unsigned object.

Scratch Expo iOS fingerprint comparison with and without the local module produced different runtime hashes. Mobile typecheck and all 28 Jest suites / 149 tests passed, including a detectOpenHandles run with clean exit.

Native callback regression executable on macOS: non-server-trust challenges use default handling without a certificate-change event; a server-trust challenge without trust/leaf cancels with an ordinary TLS failure. This does not exercise a TLS handshake.
